# Chapter Ten: The End of Happiness

> *"Your time in midworld be done, come to me and hear me praise your deeds, let me honor you with feast and drink, be my brother among the clouds."*
> — **Book of Aurtus**

Winter has come, Marcus thought standing there on the porch, his eyes following the large white flakes that lazily floated down to cover the landscape laid out before him, the familiar farm looked alien covered in the white sheet of winter snow.

A cup of hot cider held close to his body aided in combatting the cold biting into his fingers. Smiling, he felt the hot steam play over his face as he continued to survey the alabaster scene of beauty spread out before him from the porch of the small cabin.

The smile drained from his face as he turned to ensure he was still alone, Orah had not yet come to join him in there morning ritual.

A look of worry creased his brow as he turned back to the winter scene playing out before him.

His abilities had been changing, growing stronger, Marcus had first noticed the change over a month ago, at first it had been small things, his ability to feel the crystals grew steadily stronger but that had not been all, he had practiced with the book, his ability to complete the lessons became easier with each passing day, when he had started he could barely lift a pebble he recalled, looking towards the large bail of hair, Marcus closed his eyes and with a thought gathered energy to himself, using it to easily lift the bail two feet off the ground and holding it there, he let the bail go and watched as it fell to the ground with a muffled thump, his power was growing, increasing and he didn’t know what that meant or why it was happening.

As his power had grown the dreams with the blonde woman had come more frequently, somehow, they were tied and they were feeling less like dreams, becoming more real with each episode.

“Have I gone insane” he whispered opening his eyes. He had not shared this with anyone, including Orah or even Veric he wasn’t even sure how to explain it and both would needlessly worry, he had promised himself once he discovered what it was or what was happening, he would talk to them but not before he thought, he wouldn’t put this worry on anyone else until he knew for sure something was wrong and more importantly, that he could explain it.

Marcus jumped as delicate feminine hands wrapped around his chest as the cool pressure of Orah’s face leaned against his back.

A contented smile broke over his face as the worry and concern melted away, the only thing that existed at that moment was her. Orah was his happiness, his only desire was to see her face light up when she smiled.

Marcus turned looking into those big blue eyes under the bed tangled head of blonde hair. “Good morning” he whispered leaning down and kissing her soft warm lips.

Her body snuggled against him as she lay her head against his shoulder and sighed.

Marcus turned, sliding his arms gently around her and slowly running his fingers up her back, feeling her arch with pleasure as he did.

“Why don’t you go sit down, I will get us breakfast. I have a lunch date with Veric, but when I return, I want to talk” he said smiling down at her. “Nothing bad” he preempted and watched her visibly relax.

Orah huffed playfully running her hand over Marcus’s cheek turning and going back into the cabin. He turned to look out over the winter landscape one last time before entering the house.

He made breakfast and they both ate, talking about the chores and the upgrades to the farm they would need to make in the spring.

Marcus had never felt more at home or comfortable then at those simple domestic moments with Orah. Now that they were a couple, he wanted to make it official, wanted to officially become husband and wife, he would discuss it with Veric, and once he understood how to do it, he would ask her to be his.

Marcus had never been one to commit himself in a relationship, hell before Orah the longest relationship he had, was two months. But he had never felt like this for anyone else and knew, he just knew it was right.

Orah kept giving him odd looks he knew she couldn’t help but notice the idiotic grin permanently plastered across his features. But he wanted it to be a surprise.

The changes to himself that plagued his waking hours, pushed to the back of his mind as he concentrated on her, on their life together and ultimately to their happiness.

After breakfast they made love as they did most mornings. Afterwards, Marcus lay there with Orah’s long alabaster limbs wrapped around his body, warmth radiating from them giving him goosebumps, they lay there as long as they could ignoring the work that needed to get done on the farm, doing their best to forget the responsibilities that occupied there waking hours.

But as with every day the animals required tending and the trip to the general store needed to be completed as they were out of quite a few things they would need, responsibility, the harsh mistress that it was finally called out, forcing them back to the present.

Filling the basin with water Marcus stood over it with a towel washing himself Orah approached, coming to lay her head on his shoulder and wringing the towel with warm water, Marcus gently ran it over her legs and arms, finishing with her sex, getting a slight moan as he finished washing her as he kissed her neck and back, the actions threatening to take them right back to bed.

Finally, she playfully pushed him off laughing as he unsuccessfully tried to move in for yet another bout of lovemaking.

Shooting him a mock annoyed look, Orah dressed for the cold. Marcus stood there smiling, naked as he watched her finish dressing, moving towards the door, she turned and blew him a kiss before leaving into the main area of the cabin.

He heard the front door open and close as he began to dress.

As he came onto the porch he caught sight of Orah feeding the animals, he stopped and smiled, watching her laugh as she fed the pigs and with a resigned sigh, Marcus walked to the stables and saddled the younger of the two farm horses, still a novice at it, it took him longer than it should and Orah had moved further out into the farm as he rode out of the stables pointing the horse towards town.

As he left the confines of the farm’s fence line Orah came around from the side of the cabin, Marcus stopped the horse “I love you Orah, I always will” he bellowed to the smiling and radiant woman who blew him a kiss before he moved off towards town.

His thoughts turned to their life and the future as always, it eventually turned to children and then the dark troubled look came back over his face.

The project had changed him on a genetic level, whatever they used had altered his mind and body, The thrumming that kept him awake at night and his new found abilities all stemmed from that, Marcus knew sooner or later he would carry the branding of a mage, would that effect my children he thought looking to her as she continued to move around the animal pens, could he bring himself to tell her that not only did he no longer feel human but that any children they had may also receive the changes that now plagued him.

Science had not progressed again to be able to allow him to find out exactly what had been altered within him.

Every day his abilities became stronger, the senses that had begun to manifest that day in the forest had matured to the point he could no longer ignore them, he would have to tell her, tonight he thought, tonight I will sit down and explain to her everything, she needs to know before I ask her to spend her life with me, to have children. He thought.

He rode for hours, lost in his thoughts, finally coming to the front gates of the town, he spied the guards and waved smiling at the two bundled soldiers.

“Ho Kanin how goes it?” he said getting a smile from the shorter of the two guards, “Ho Marcus, Sperig cheated again in slugs, but the crooked fool won’t admit to it” he said nodding towards the taller guard, Sperig shook his head “He is a sore loser, don’t listen to him Marcus” he said poking his friend with a chuckle.

“How is the farm Marcus” Kanin asked and Marcus smiled “Amazing my friend, amazing” he answered tying up the horse and entering the gate of the small village “I am going to visit Messenger Veric, I am sure if I asked he would allow me to bring you back some hot cider if you want” he said.

Sperig looked from him to the keep and for a moment he looked as if he would accept but then he shook his head and his face fell “Thank you Marcus, your kindness would rival that of Aurtus, but we are not permitted drink on duty” he sighed. Marcus nodded commiserating “I understand, your dedication to duty honors Aurtus my friend” he answered.

Since coming to live with these people he had done his best to learn not only the language but the idioms that would allow him to blend in better. He smiled as he mentally patted himself on the back for that one.

Sperig smiled and slightly bowed. “Have a good visit my friend” he answered, and Marcus entered the village, trudging carefully through the snow as he made his way to the stone keep.

Up on the hill in the distance he could see the outline of the Lord Seer’s fort overlooking the village and the territory. The Specter of authority that all in the village lived under, a reminder that they were ruled and to their place in this world he considered as the smile slightly faltered.

He had heard stories of the lords and their proclivities, the moral of most of them being ’it is best that they do not notice you’. It had been a month and a half since his altercation with the tax collectors but since then nothing had come of it and he had begun to breathe easier.

But when he came to town and looked upon the fort on the hill, he wondered if the Lord Seer might not already know his name.

“Ho Marcus, it is cold my friend, hurry so I can stop being a good host” called Veric from the doorway interrupting Marcus’s thoughts. He waved at the old Messenger “Ho Veric, I am coming as fast as I can, keep your robe on” he said both men smiling at each other.

As Marcus came into the keep both men embraced each other “It is very good to see you Marcus, it has been a week and I have so much to tell you” Veric said excitedly.

He loved complaining about his flock and some of the idiotic things they got up to. Judging by his excitement someone had finally beat the story of Old man Jorun getting caught with the sheep by his wife.

Marcus still cringed at that story and Veric loved retelling it almost every time he came.

The Messenger guided him into his private chambers, entering in front of the old man he noticed the cider was already on the warmer and Veric had laid out bread and butter on the table.

Taking off his coat Marcus hung the fur covered Jacket on the hook behind the door and removed the waterproofed leather boots as well. The Messenger motioned for him to sit and Marcus obeyed.

Taking the seat across from his friend as both men settled at the small table. Veric pulled a plate and putting fresh bread and a pat of butter on it, handing the plate to Marcus.

The old messenger kept looking at him oddly as he did this, finally Marcus, almost defensively and asked “what?”.

Veric just smiled “You have the oddest look on your face, as if you are bursting over to tell me something” he commented, Marcus shook his head.

His friend knew him too well. After Veric had served both of them bread and cider Marcus took a good long pull of the hot liquid, then looking at Veric he organized his thoughts as the other man waited patiently.

“I need to know what the steps are to have a wedding” he stated and Veric arched an eyebrow “I take it this isn’t another one of your theoretical scenarios” Veric questioned.

Marcus shook his head “I am going to ask Orah to become my wife Veric” he stated and the old man lit up as a smile spread across his face “Well Aurtus be praised it is about time, I thought I might have to tell her to beat you over the head before you decided to make it official” he stated, getting excited.

“There is a lot we have to do my friend, I mean the wedding itself is simple, but we need to send out invitations and did you get her the necklace?” he asked and Marcus’s face fell “Necklace?” he asked concerned.

Veric nodded, “You can’t ask her unless you have the necklace, it’s a promise before the gods of your intent” he said, he turned and got up, practically rushing to the drawers and chests in the corner of the room.

Veric began to rummage through them, throwing things over his shoulder Marcus had to dodge a book and two robes as he was searching. Finally, with a shout of delight Veric turned holding a simple chain with what looked like a silver sword on it.

“Here it is” he said walking gently over to the table and laying it down” Marcus eyed the necklace; it was a beautifully crafted piece of jewelry.

“Oh Veric, that looks expensive, I don’t have the silverlings for something like that, the farm didn’t do all that well this season” he said pushing the necklace back towards his friend.

Veric huffed, “I am not selling it to you, I am giving it to you my friend, you cannot ask her without it and damn if you are going to make that woman wait another day” he said almost insulted at Marcus’s gesture.

Sighing he gently picked up the necklace, knowing he wasn’t going to win the argument with this stubborn old man. Marcus put it in his small coin purse “Thank you Veric, I mean it, marrying her means the world to me” he said, and the old man beamed again.

“I know Marcus, I have known since the first time I saw you two together, I will take care of all the arrangements for the ceremony, we will have it at the first sign of spring, it will be the most amazing wedding since the Empress herself was married” he said.

The old man seemed to explode with energy, his attitude infectious and soon Marcus found himself smiling excitedly as they discussed the plans and the ceremony.

They talked well into the middle of the day, Marcus finally having to beg off but promising to return in a few days to finish planning.

It is possible he thought that Veric was more excited than he was about the wedding, making his way to the general store, he gave a greeting to the old shopkeeper and then began collecting items and placing them at the front of the store, pulling a small list from his pocket he reviewed it carefully, checking it against the items now lined up on the counter, mostly things like flour and bolts of cloth as well as thread and a new knife, items they could not craft but where critical in forging ahead on the farm.

He pulled out fifteen silverlings out of his pouch, careful not to lose the necklace Veric had given him, paying for the items, he bought a small square of cloth, using it to wrap the supplies and sling them over his shoulder, he returned to his horse, bidding the guards farewell as he mounted the old farm animal and with a smile he left the village for home, he had purposely not gone into the mages shop, avoiding it this trip as he did not have any reason to be there, and didn’t need the knowing looks the old mage would give him.

Picking up his pace a little in order to make it back to the farm before dusk, his mind reeled with thoughts of the wedding and his life with Orah.

He chastised himself knowing that Orah would be worried when he didn’t return in time for dinner, he would have to make it up to her he thought.

Marcus was lost in his thoughts when he first smelled the acrid smoke, it came on the wind, at first sporadic but the closer he progressed towards the farm the heavier the smell became.

Looking around he couldn’t understand where it was coming from and then he looked forward, a chill running down his back “Oh, no, no no,” he whispered seeing the lone pillar of black smoke coming from the direction of the small cabin.

He coaxed the horse faster not taking his eyes off the pillar of roiling black smoke as it rose to the heavens.

Approaching the farm, he heard a commotion coming from the direction of the cabin as he listened, he could hear the agitated calls of the animals echoing over the pass.

Pushing the old beast even faster, the horse protesting loudly, he turned the corner of trees allowing him to view the farm, his blood ran cold as the entire cabin stood engulfed in flames.

Jumping off the old horse he barreled through the tree-ensconced area that separated the pass from the house, branches ripped at his clothes and face, but he took no notice, his eyes never leaving the flame laden roof of his home.

Exploding from the tree line, he could see the gathering of horses and knew even before he could see them, what had happened.

He had let them live, the tax collectors, despite the threats he had let them live, he had payed them, and he had sent them on their way, but the egos could not resolve what had been done to them, so they had returned, but not to collect a tax.

His lungs were burning, and his legs were aching, but Marcus pushed harder and faster, seeing the flames crawling from the windows and licking at the old thatch roof.

He saw the gathering of people before they saw him. He ran by them, surprised yells going up from the small crowd, his only thought on saving the woman he loved.

Bursting through the door and into a wall of smoke. He reeled, his eyes burning as he pushed forward. Coughing he tried to peer through the smoke but couldn’t see his hand in front of his face. “ORAH” he yelled, dropping to the ground and crawling to try and see past the smoke and flames.

He couldn’t see her, couldn’t hear her, frantically he looked around the main room, not finding any sign of her, he could see the couch alit with flame and through the open door he made out the bed. Stopping his eyes coming to the bundle wrapped up there.

He scurried across the floor, ignoring the heat and pain, blinking his eyes as tears ran freely his body trying to get rid of the irritation of the smoke.

Finally reaching the bed; he watched in horror as the entire topside went up in flames. Grabbing a blanket off the floor he threw it on top of the bed covering the silhouette of his love, desperately, frantically trying to smother growing flames.

The fire bit at his body, ignoring the pain he continued to smother the flames until they were out revealing the burnt smoking bundle lying on top of the bed.

The house burned around him as he gently picked up the bundle, cradling it in his arms like a newborn child as he carried the unmoving remains in his arms, somewhere in his mind he knew she was dead.

He knew no one could have lived through that but still he lovingly stroked the silhouette of her head under the blanket, unable to remove it, to see her dead eyes staring back at him, instead he cooed and whispered as the chaos of destruction played around him, Marcus told her he loved her and that everything would be okay.

He continued to ignore the chaos as the house began to collapse around him, it didn’t matter, he had to get Orah out of the house, he had to get her to the lawn, then he could wake her up, then she would come to and tell him how much she loved him, how happy she was he had come into her life.

He stumbled through the door and into the evening light of day as the roof finally collapsed behind him.

Walking onto the porch he found himself in the center of the ring of men as they stood there, hands playing over the butts of pistols and carriage guns fastened onto their hips, like gunslingers from an old western movie he thought randomly.

“Hello, again, Dirt born, sorry about your girl, we got a little rough” one of the men laughed pulling the pistol and waving it towards the burning house.

The others joined in with the laughter as they all took a menacing step towards him. “You should have heard her beg and scream before we lit the sow on fire” said another, Marcus also recognizing him as one of the two collectors he had allowed to live.

The voices seemed to fade as his heartbeat pounded in his ear drums as he stood detached, absently stroking the head of the woman he loved, somewhere in his mind, something broke as a scream echoed distantly, it took him a moment to realize, It had come from him, the group of men stepping back, the smiles leaving their face as the rage infused scream erupted from his body.

Marcus didn’t understand, didn’t know what was happening as power, like a river flowed into his body, he felt the swelling of the energy as he collected more and more of it, he felt as if he would burst and just as he thought he could take no more, thought that his body would explode with energy, it shot out from him, in six bright blue pillars, slamming into the men and as he watched in horror, they erupted into micro suns, the fire so bright that Marcus had to close his eyes for fear of going blind, there was no time for the men to scream, no time for them to react, they just simply stood there, burning for a moment until their bodies simply crumbled to the ground, piles of now smoking meat.

He stood there gawking at the remains and suddenly a blue flash nearly blinded him as pain seared his shoulder, turning he found a last man standing there with his pistol, Marcus had not seen him and that had probably saved his live he thought detached, the man staring in shock and horror at Marcus.

He felt broken, part of his mind raged to exact vengeance for the woman now laying in his arms, but another part looked over the destruction, You did this, you killed these men, without a thought you ended six lives, you are a monster. The voice in his head spoke, his shoulders slumped as he considered this and before the man could fire again, Marcus merely looked his way and the gun disintegrated, breaking down to metal and wood dust right before him.

The stared for a moment, frozen in shock, before he gained control of himself and bolting back towards the road he simply ran past his horse and up the road.

“No” Marcus croaked, he had to explain to the man that he wasn’t a monster, that he didn’t do this.

Taking two steps his body taxed both mentally and physically collapsed as darkness descended over his conscious mind,

Orah still in his arms.
